known_installation_note: The installation is patched in five other tracked files. This header matches both author HEAD and installed prefix byte-for-byte. No clean whole-installation or binary reproduction claim.

facts.fact: ExecAsyncFuncContext stores std::future<void>. TryPull tests wait_for(std::chrono::seconds(0)) == std::future_status::ready and returns that boolean; no wait-until-completion loop.
The separate ExecuteAsyncFuncPull method calls task.wait(), which is the blocking variant. It is not the TryPull call used here.

ExecuteAsyncFuncPush creates a packaged_task<void()>, obtains its future, enqueues a wrapper that executes the task, signals workers and returns the context. This is an explicitly queued packaged-task future, not a deferred std::async future.

Project ready()/ready_blocks() call TryPull. collect() and collect_ready() require readiness before task.get(). The submitted background callable invokes ExecuteFunction; its execution can wait on author/model work without making TryPull itself a model wait. Task failure may also make the future ready; get() then propagates that exception.

deadline_implication: The existing 10-second per-command timeout must not be described as a 10-second model-completion wait merely because poll uses TryPull: TryPull is a zero-duration readiness probe. IPC transfer, queue/lock acquisition, result serialization and other command paths are separate; this narrow source check does not prove every whole command always finishes within10seconds or certify the pending optional query-deadline change.
